# Reporting and reproducibility

::: {.learning-objectives}
**Learning objectives**

- Preserve every analytical decision required to reproduce a map.
- Report bibliometric methods without overstating conclusions.
- Create a minimum quality-assurance checklist.
:::

## Reproducible project layers

| Layer | Retain |
|---|---|
| Raw data | Original exports and checksums |
| Search | Full strings, dates, platforms, filters, counts |
| Screening | Decisions, reasons, reviewers, conflict resolution |
| Cleaning | Dictionaries, mappings, duplicate log |
| Parameters | Fields, thresholds, algorithms, normalisation, seed |
| Derived data | Cleaned records, networks, membership tables |
| Outputs | Figures, tables, and validation sheets |
| Environment | R, package, Quarto, and operating-system versions |

## Lock the analytical environment

```r
install.packages("renv")
renv::init()
renv::snapshot()
```

Record the session:

```{r}
#| label: reproducibility-session

sessionInfo()
```

This matters because thematic algorithms and returned objects can change between package versions.

## Parameter register

```{r}
#| label: reproducibility-parameters

source(here::here("R", "00_setup.R"))
M <- load_demo_data()
M <- M |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    DE = stringr::str_to_upper(stringr::str_squish(DE)),
    ID = stringr::str_to_upper(stringr::str_squish(ID))
  )
M <- bibliometrix::mergeKeywords(M, force = TRUE)
tm <- bibliometrix::thematicMap(
  M = M,
  field = "KW_Merged",
  n = 100,
  minfreq = 5,
  ngrams = 1,
  stemming = FALSE,
  size = 0.7,
  n.labels = 3,
  community.repulsion = 0,
  repel = TRUE,
  remove.terms = fcm_remove_terms,
  synonyms = fcm_synonyms,
  cluster = "louvain",
  subgraphs = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.5,
  seed = 20261126
)

tm$params
```

Export this table with every final map.

## Minimum validation checks

```{r}
#| label: reproducibility-checks

validation_checks <- tibble::tribble(
  ~check, ~expected,
  "Unique DOI among non-missing DOI values", TRUE,
  "Publication year within protocol range", TRUE,
  "All included records have title", TRUE,
  "Thematic field completeness reported", TRUE,
  "Cited-reference completeness reported", TRUE,
  "Cluster labels checked by two reviewers", TRUE,
  "Sensitivity analysis completed", TRUE,
  "Citation snapshot date reported", TRUE,
  "Package versions retained", TRUE
)

validation_checks
```

## Suggested methods wording

> Bibliographic records were converted into a standard bibliographic data frame using the `bibliometrix` R package. Author and indexed keywords were audited and harmonised using a prespecified thesaurus. Query-defining drug terms were removed from clustering because they did not discriminate among topics. The conceptual structure was examined using an association-strength-normalised keyword co-occurrence network and community detection. Themes were positioned by centrality and density, and automatic labels were verified against leading terms and high-membership publications. Sensitivity analyses varied the keyword field, term threshold, number of retained terms, and clustering algorithm. Package versions, seeds, parameter tables, and cleaning dictionaries were retained.

Adapt this wording to the actual procedure. Never claim independent dual review, prespecification, or full-text verification unless it occurred.

## Reporting guidance

Use BIBLIO as preliminary bibliometric reporting guidance and PRISMA-S for applicable search-reporting elements [@montazeri2023; @rethelefsen2021]. Neither checklist replaces a study-specific protocol.

## Claims to avoid

- “The most cited article was the best study.”
- “The lower-left topic is definitely emerging.”
- “A country produced the study participants.”
- “No funding metadata means no funding.”
- “The cluster proves a causal relationship.”
- “Low publication volume proves an unmet clinical need.”

## Exercise

Audit one published bibliometric paper using the validation checks above. Identify one missing parameter that prevents exact replication.
